title: Adaptive Tutor Strategy Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Explanations, hints, diagnostic questions, and outcomes across learner difficulties. The Adaptive Tutor Strategy Database documents the moves a good tutor makes: when to explain vs when to hint, how to diagnose the actual misunderstanding (not just the wrong answer), and what to do about each difficulty. Each strategy record covers the learner difficulty it addresses, the tutor moves (explanation, hint sequence, diagnostic question, worked example), and the measured outcome — because tutoring strategies are hypotheses until tested.

title: Adaptive Tutor Strategy Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tutoring anatomy: DIAGNOSE (what is the learner actually thinking? — the error is data, not failure) -> SELECT MOVE (explanation for missing knowledge, hints for stuck-but-close, questions for misconceptions, examples for pattern-building) -> EXECUTE (one move at a time, then check) -> VERIFY (new item, same difficulty — did it transfer?). Hint design: graduated (general -> specific), never give away the answer before the learner attempts; fading (reduce help as competence grows). Explanation design: connect to prior knowledge, one idea per explanation, check understanding before moving on. Misconception handling: elicit the wrong idea explicitly, create cognitive conflict (a case where it fails), then build the correct model. Feedback: immediate for procedures, delayed for concepts; specific and actionable.

demo.title: Execution: Bayesian knowledge tracing update
demo.code: let pL=0.3;const pT=0.2,pS=0.1,pG=0.25;function update(correct){const pC=pL*(1-pS)+(1-pL)*pG;const pLgiven=correct?(pL*(1-pS)/pC):(pL*pS/(pL*pS+(1-pL)*(1-pG)));pL=pLgiven+(1-pLgiven)*pT;return pL;}const responses=[1,1,0,1,1];const traj=responses.map(update);const mastered=traj[traj.length-1]>=0.95;J({final:+traj[traj.length-1].toFixed(3),mastered});assert(traj.every(v=>v>=0&&v<=1),'bkt-range');assert(traj[traj.length-1]>0.3,'bkt-learn');

demo.title: Verification: concept graph is a DAG
demo.code: const edges=[['arith','algebra'],['algebra','deriv'],['deriv','backprop']];const nodes=[...new Set(edges.flat())];function topo(){const indeg={};nodes.forEach(n=>indeg[n]=0);edges.forEach(([a,b])=>indeg[b]++);const q=nodes.filter(n=>indeg[n]===0);const order=[];while(q.length){const n=q.shift();order.push(n);edges.filter(e=>e[0]===n).forEach(([a,b])=>{if(--indeg[b]===0)q.push(b);});}return order;}const order=topo();J({order,isDAG:order.length===nodes.length});assert(order.length===nodes.length&&order.indexOf('arith')<order.indexOf('backprop'),'dag');

title: Adaptive Tutor Strategy Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: matching test (errors map to documented misconceptions); move test (selections fit the diagnosis rules); hint test (sequences graduate and fade); determinism test. Limitations: misconception catalogs are subject-specific; outcomes need real studies; strategies advise, tutors decide. Every strategy carries its evidence grade.
